messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: ggplot2 derivative: aov_plot()
parts:
Hi all,

My colleagues lament the passing of StatView, an OS 9 app that
provided rather simple yet powerful abilities to plot data for a given
effect from a factorial ANOVA. To facilitate their conversion to R,
I've attempted to replicate this in a function called aov_plot().

I'd be interested to get input from anyone that might find this
interesting/useful. I've uploaded the current version of the code to:
http://drop.io/aov_plot

- aov_plot.R contains the code and description of aov_plot()

- demo.R contains a demo of using aov_plot on data similar to that
obtained from the Attention Network Test

- generate_demo_data.R contains code for generating data necessary for
running demo.R

Note that the default error bars I've chosen represent Fisher's Least
Significant Difference. In the context of purely within or between
effects, these bars facilitate post-hoc multiple comparison (if the
bars of any two points fail to overlap, the points may be considered
significantly different at alpha=.05). However, I've been told that
they can not be used in this manner in the context of mixed between &
within effects. In absence of consensus on an alternative for these
cases, I chose to plot the FLSD bars but suggest that use of such
plots should also contain a footnote noting that the bars can not be
used for post-hoc multiple comparison. In the future I may change my
mind on this and instead simply plot no error bars in such
circumstances.

Cheers,

Mike

Yes, the problem is that the standard error of the means maybe almost
completely unrelated to the standard errors of the differences between
the means (generally because of blocking type effects). I've played
around a little with multcompView package to supplement these plots
with the classical group letters, so you can easily see if two groups
are different. You still need to figure out which comparisons are of
most interest.

(I think this general problem is a really interesting research problem)
